title: The Figure a Revised Offer Stands At on Northbeam Renew Trade-In
content:
**The figure.** Where an appraisal finds a batch other than the condition declared, a revised offer is owed to the customer and is put at the amount the appraisal supports, rounded to the cent. The amount the appraisal supports is the figure the appraisal recorded on the agreement, which covers the devices booked in and whatever deductions the bench found on them.

**The order the figure is reached in.** The revised offer is worked out in one order and no other: it starts from the figure the gap treatment reaches, the cover deduction is then taken off that figure, and the ageing markdown is applied last to what that step leaves; the figure is rounded to the cent and never falls below nothing. The markdown is a percentage of what the step before it leaves, not of the figure the offer started from, and what remains is that figure less that percentage of it; the rounding to the cent is done once, at the end.

**Worked figure on hypothetical inputs.** Take a Northbeam Renew Trade-In agreement whose appraisal recorded an amount of 1836.40 USD supported on the devices booked in.

1. The figure the offer starts from is the amount the appraisal supports, 1836.40 USD.
2. Nothing is taken off that figure as a cover deduction, so 1836.40 USD stands.
3. No ageing markdown is applied to what that step leaves, so 1836.40 USD stands.
4. Rounded to the cent, the revised offer is 1836.40 USD.

Had the figure come out below nothing at the end it would stand at nothing, the offer never falling below nothing.

**Where the figure comes from.** The amount the appraisal supports is read from the appraised amount standing on the agreement itself, and covers the devices booked in against that agreement together with whatever deductions the bench found on them; it is not worked out afresh from the quote.
